To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sCO2 cycles offer significant cost and performance benefits in GTCC heat recovery systems.
sCO2 based GTCC heat recovery cycles can provide lower installed cost, lower O&M, and lower LCOE than steam based GTCC.
sCO2 heat engines can be cost effectively applied to GTCC systems, and that the LCOE of these systems is lower than that of conventional GTCCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of sCO2 based power systems for heat recovery applications.
the development of sCO2 power cycles and heat recovery systems for distributed and utility scale power generation.
the design and optimization of sCO2 based power cycles for GTCC and other heat recovery applications, with a focus on system cost.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sCO2 based GTCC power generation is economically superior to steam systems over the entire size range studied.
the sCO2 cycle has a lower installed cost and lower LCOE than steam cycle for GTCC applications over the range of power sizes studied.
sCO2 heat rejection systems offer a compelling alternative to steam based systems for GTCC power generation across a broad range of sizes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of sCO2 in bottoming and heat extraction applications can provide significant cost and performance benefits for a wide range of power system applications, and that the EPS100 sCO2 heat engine represents the first commercially viable technology to exploit these benefits.
the use of sCO2 as a working fluid in closed cycle power conversion systems can offer substantial cost advantages over the use of steam in GTCC power plants.

sCO2 cycles can be used to improve the efficiency and cost of gas turbine power plants, and that these cycles can be used as an effective technology for heat recovery and waste heat to power applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sCO2 heat engines offer significant advantages over steam based Rankine cycles, and are particularly well-suited to heat recovery applications.
sCO2 cycles can be designed to compete with steam cycles in both performance and cost.

sCO2 based heat recovery cycles can be designed for GTCC power plants at a lower cost and with better performance than comparable steam systems, across the full range from distributed generation to utility scale.
